title: Bigo earthworks
description: Cattle-keeping people dig several kilometres of ditches and banks, the largest earthworks of the lakes region and linked by tradition to the Chwezi rulers.

title: Speke reaches the source of the Nile
description: After months at the court of Kabaka Mutesa I, John Hanning Speke sees the Nile leaving Lake Victoria.

title: Stanley at the court of Mutesa
description: Henry Morton Stanley visits the kabaka and sends a letter calling for missionaries, who arrive two years later.

title: Uganda Martyrs
description: Kabaka Mwanga II has Christian converts among his pages burned to death, the largest of a series of executions.

title: Battle of Mengo
description: Frederick Lugard's Maxim gun decides a fight between Protestant and Catholic factions in favour of the Protestants and the British company.

title: British protectorate
description: Britain takes over Buganda from the Imperial British East Africa Company and declares the Uganda Protectorate.

title: Mwanga deposed
description: Kabaka Mwanga II rebels against British control, is defeated and is replaced by his infant son Daudi Chwa.

title: Buganda Agreement
description: The regents of Buganda accept British rule in return for self-government and freehold land for the chiefs, giving the kingdom a special place in the protectorate.

title: Makerere founded
description: A technical school opens that becomes the leading university of East Africa.

title: Kabaka Mutesa II deported
description: The governor exiles the king of Buganda for opposing British plans, setting off a crisis that ends with his return two years later.

title: Owen Falls Dam opened
description: Queen Elizabeth II opens a hydroelectric dam on the Nile where it leaves Lake Victoria.

title: Independence
description: Uganda becomes independent from Britain with Milton Obote as prime minister.

title: Attack on the kabaka's palace
description: Troops under Idi Amin storm the palace on Obote's orders, the kabaka flees abroad, and the kingdoms are abolished the next year.

title: Idi Amin seizes power
description: The army commander overthrows Obote while he is abroad and begins eight years of rule in which several hundred thousand people are killed.

title: Expulsion of Asians
description: Amin orders the country's people of South Asian origin, about 80,000 in number, to leave within ninety days.

title: Entebbe raid
description: Israeli commandos free the passengers of a hijacked airliner held with Amin's support.

title: Fall of Kampala
description: Tanzanian troops and Ugandan exiles take the capital and end Amin's rule, six months after he had invaded Tanzania.

title: Bush War begins
description: After a disputed election returns Obote to power, Yoweri Museveni's guerrillas attack an army barracks and begin a five-year war.

title: Museveni takes Kampala
description: The National Resistance Army captures the capital and Yoweri Museveni becomes president.

title: Buganda kingdom restored
description: Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II is crowned kabaka after the government allows the traditional kingdoms to return as cultural institutions.

title: New constitution
description: A constitution drafted after wide consultation comes into force, keeping Museveni's no-party system for the time being.

title: Barlonyo massacre
description: The Lord's Resistance Army kills some 300 people in a camp for the displaced, one of the worst attacks of its long war in the north.

title: Multiparty politics restored
description: A referendum ends the ban on party activity, in the same year that parliament removes the limit on presidential terms.

title: Kampala bombings
description: Bombs set by the Somali group al-Shabaab kill 74 people watching the football World Cup final.
